query: Wang Yi China Foreign Minister visit South Korea 2026 postponed Taiwan dispute rescheduled July August 2026
answer:
I've completed the research. Here's a summary of the key findings on Wang Yi's visit to South Korea and the Taiwan dispute:

## Key Findings

**The dispute (April 2026):** Wang Yi's prospective visit to Seoul was effectively put on hold over a Taiwan-labeling dispute. On **March 31, 2026**, South Korea removed the "China (Taiwan)" label from its electronic arrival cards (to satisfy Taiwan's complaints). On **April 14, 2026**, China's foreign ministry objected, reaffirming the "one China" principle. Around **April 20-21**, Seoul said no visit arrangements had been finalized and called the arrival-card change "a simple administrative and technical adjustment." China also reportedly declined a visit by South Korea's spy chief amid the same tensions.

**Rescheduling status (July 2026):** By the most recent reporting (**July 14, 2026**), Korea and China had resumed "close working-level consultations" and were discussing a possible Wang visit **"as early as next month" (August 2026)**. However — importantly — **the visit was NOT confirmed** as of mid-July 2026; it remained in the discussion stage with no finalized date.

**On the July/August framing in your question:** No evidence of a July 2026 visit; **August 2026 was the earliest prospective window under discussion**, but unconfirmed.

**Context:** Wang last visited Korea in November 2023. Seoul framed the potential visit as follow-up to a Korea-China summit (Lee Jae Myung–Xi Jinping) and groundwork for a possible Xi visit to Seoul.

**Caveat:** AskNews tools were unavailable (inactive subscription), so findings rely on web searches of Korea Times, SCMP, UPI, and Chinese MFA reporting. No source confirmed the visit actually took place.

key_facts: Wang Yi's prospective visit to Seoul was put on hold in April 2026 over a Taiwan-labeling dispute concerning South Korea's electronic arrival cards.
On March 31, 2026, South Korea removed departure/destination fields (eliminating the 'China (Taiwan)' label) from its electronic arrival card after Taiwan complained about the wording.
On April 14, 2026, China's foreign ministry objected, stating 'Taiwan is part of China' and reaffirming the 'one China' principle.
Around April 20-21, 2026, Seoul said no specific arrangements had been finalized for Wang's visit and called the arrival-card change 'a simple administrative and technical adjustment.'
China also reportedly declined/blocked a visit by South Korea's spy chief (National Intelligence Service director) amid the same Taiwan tensions in April 2026.
As of July 14, 2026, Korea and China were in 'close working-level consultations' over a possible Wang visit 'as early as next month' (August 2026).
The Wang visit was NOT confirmed as of mid-July 2026 — it remained in the discussion/consultation stage with no finalized date.
FM Cho Hyun originally sought a one-on-one meeting with Wang in Q1 2026, but that timeframe passed without a meeting.
Wang Yi last visited Korea in November 2023 for a trilateral Korea-China-Japan foreign ministers' meeting.
Wang visited North Korea (Pyongyang) around April 8-12, 2026, meeting Kim Jong Un, shortly before the Korea impasse hardened.
Seoul framed the potential visit as follow-up to a Korea-China summit (Lee Jae Myung and Xi Jinping) and groundwork for a possible Xi visit to Seoul.
